script.base: No spread or total is saved, so this is inferred only from weeks 2-4 form: a competitive, pass-live game rather than a slog or a declared blowout. ARI's pass defense leaks in every zone (YPA left 9.36, middle 8.74, right 9.10) and blitzes only 24%, while DET's offense is positive either way (EPA/db 0.34 vs blitz, 0.19 vs none), so Goff should keep throwing to St. Brown (32 targets, 236 yards L3), LaPorta, TeSlaa and Williams. DET's own own run fit is the soft side (4.72 YPC, 16 runs of 10+), but DET also blitzes 31% into an ARI offense that is bad when blitzed (EPA/db -0.39 vs blitz, +0.13 vs none), so Love stays involved only while the game stays within a score.
script.flip1: DET gets up big, kills the clock with Gibbs (L3 already 51 carries), and TeSlaa's deep shots stall the way a clock-kill stalls QB/WR yards; ARI then abandons Love (44 carries L3) and dumps to Wilson/McBride/Bourne in garbage time.
script.flip2: ARI controls the ball on the ground against DET's 4.72 YPC run defense, DET's missing center Cade Mays and guard Ben Bartch stall Gibbs, and the game slows so explosive receiving (TeSlaa 66/95, Williams 102) does not show up.

matchup.pressure: ARI blitz rate 24% and DET is better when blitzed (EPA/db 0.34) than when not (0.19), so ARI pressure is not the deep-shot killer. DET blitz rate 31% and ARI is poor vs blitz (EPA/db -0.39) and fine when not blitzed (+0.13); pressure that gets home should cut Wilson's air-yard efficiency (335 air, only 202 yards on 37 targets) and funnel ARI toward McBride/Love checkdowns.
matchup.bleeds: ARI bleeds the pass, not the run (rush YPC allowed 4.24, only 11 runs of 10+ in 4 games, but 14 passes of 20+ for 117 yards). DET bleeds the run (4.72 YPC, 16 runs of 10+) and the middle of the field (11.52 YPA), with 20 passes of 20+ for 179 yards.
matchup.overlap: TeSlaa's downfield role (215 air yards / 16 targets, about 13.4 aDOT) overlaps the ARI secondary bleed plus Wingard out. Gibbs does not overlap a run bleed: ARI's 4.24 YPC is the sturdier side of that defense, and DET is without Mays and Bartch. McBride (33 targets) overlaps DET's middle bleed, but his line is 84.5 vs 49 yards/game L3, so that overlap is not a priced edge.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. TeSlaa lost because the market was right to hang 25.5 on a boom/bust depth receiver: the 0 is still in the last four, 215 air yards did not convert once Goff checked down to St. Brown (32 targets), LaPorta (24) and Gibbs (23) against a 24% blitz that never forced the deep ball, and Wingard's replacement sat on the one shot. Gibbs under lost because DET led, the clock-kill the missing spread might have been telling us about showed up, and 20-plus carries at even a modest YPC cleared 91.5 the way 156 and 99 already did, with Nolen either out or irrelevant. That counter-case is stronger on Gibbs than on TeSlaa, which is why Gibbs stays a lean and why a DET-blowout slip is the wrong stack.
slip_story: One story only: competitive pass-funnel, not a DET clock-kill and not a weather under (weather not saved). TeSlaa recyds over and Gibbs rushyds under win together if DET throws into the ARI secondary leak and does not hand Gibbs a 22-carry closeout. They lose together if DET blows ARI out and runs. Do not add Love rush over (needs ARI to stay on schedule), McBride or Wilson overs (need the DET-blitz script to fail and a yardage spike the lines already tax), or any total. Two legs, no TDs, no second market on either player.
